Financial services · Client onboarding · Redtail

How Team Financial Strategies cut new-client onboarding from 45 minutes to under 5

Firm
Team Financial Strategies
Size
4 advisors, Abilene, Texas
Contact
Jody Team, founding partner
CRM
Redtail
Project length
2 weeks
Outcome
45 minutes → under 5 minutes per new-client onboarding

The problem

Team Financial Strategies, like most independent RIAs in their size bracket, ran new-client onboarding on a hybrid paper, PDF and CRM workflow. A new prospect coming on board meant:

  • Paper or PDF intake forms: about 7 pages of personal, financial, beneficiary and risk-tolerance data
  • An operations manager re-typing the data into Redtail one field at a time (about 25 minutes per client)
  • Schwab custodian-of-record forms signed one by one in DocuSign
  • A risk-tolerance questionnaire scored on a calculator
  • An IPS drafted from a Word template by hand

The total: roughly 45 minutes per new-client onboarding, at a firm where the founding partner ends up doing the last leg of it personally.

The pain was not that this workflow was broken. The pain was that the firm could not scale it. Each new advisor meant another set of clients and another bottleneck on the operations manager's afternoon.

What we built

In 2 weeks, MonkFlow built:

  1. Custom intake form. Branded to TFS and hosted on a TFS-controlled subdomain. 28 fields with conditional logic (joint or individual, employed or retired, beneficiary tree). Document upload for driver's licenses and trust documents. E-signature on submission.
  2. Redtail auto-sync. On submission, the Contact record is created in Redtail with all 28 fields populated. Household relationships are built automatically, and the custom fields the firm uses for client segmentation are filled from the form answers.
  3. Signed-PDF generation. The Schwab account application, beneficiary designation, IPS and the firm's own engagement letter are pre-filled from the intake data and bundled into a single signing flow. Signed PDFs are archived to the Redtail client folder automatically.
  4. Compliance trail. Every form submission, sync and signature is logged with a timestamp and IP address. Partial-field detection stops incomplete intakes from reaching the CIO's inbox.

The result

Onboarding time: 45 minutes → under 5 minutes.

That is 5 minutes for the operations manager to review the auto-populated record, not to do the work. The form does the work.

Other downstream wins:

  • Funding speed: new accounts now fund within 2 business days of signing, compared with 5 to 7 days under the old workflow, where paperwork often came back not in good order.
  • Compliance: Jody can pull a complete audit trail for any new client in under 30 seconds.
  • New-client experience: clients fill in the intake on their own schedule, often before the kickoff meeting, so the meeting itself is about strategy and not paperwork.

What we'd do differently

The intake form's conditional logic was over-engineered in the first version. We shipped 9 conditional branches when 4 would have covered 95% of client types. The firm's operations manager flagged it during the first week live, and we collapsed the branches the following week.

Lesson: ship fewer branches, and add them only when clients actually hit edge cases.

Where the same pattern applies

The shape of this project is not specific to wealth management: a guided digital intake, validation before anything is accepted, automatic sync to the system of record, pre-filled documents for signature, and an audit trail. The same pattern fits:

  • LP and investor subscription onboarding at funds
  • Borrower document collection for commercial loans
  • KYC and beneficial ownership collection at banks

The results above are from Team Financial Strategies only. We do not claim them for other industries.
